ne-ESB.name: Dhekelia Cantonment
ne-ESB.note: A UK Sovereign Base Area retained when Cyprus became independent in 1960.

ne-USG.name: Guantanamo Bay Naval Base
ne-USG.note: Leased to the United States since 1903; Cuba considers the lease invalid.

ne-BRI.name: Brazilian Island
ne-BRI.note: A river island claimed by both Brazil and Uruguay.

ne-CNM.name: United Nations Buffer Zone in Cyprus
ne-CNM.note: The UN buffer zone (Green Line) between the Republic of Cyprus and Northern Cyprus, patrolled by UNFICYP since 1974.

ne-KAS.name: Siachen Glacier
ne-KAS.note: Held by India since 1984; claimed by Pakistan.

ne-KAB.name: Baikonur
ne-KAB.note: Leased to Russia by Kazakhstan for the Baikonur Cosmodrome; administered by Russia until 2050.

ne-WSB.name: Akrotiri Sovereign Base Area
ne-WSB.note: A UK Sovereign Base Area retained when Cyprus became independent in 1960.

ne-SPI.name: Southern Patagonian Ice Field
ne-SPI.note: A stretch of the Chile-Argentina border that has never been demarcated.

ne-BRT.name: Bir Tawil
ne-BRT.note: Terra nullius: claimed by neither Egypt nor Sudan, because each claims the Hala'ib Triangle instead under a different boundary line.

ne-ATA.name: Antarctica
ne-ATA.note: No state exercises sovereignty. Seven territorial claims are held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959), and research stations are operated by around 30 countries.

ne-PGA.name: Wake Island
ne-PGA.note: Individual reefs and islands are occupied by China, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Taiwan.

ne-BJN.name: Bajo Nuevo Bank
ne-BJN.note: Awarded to Colombia by the International Court of Justice in 2012.

ne-SER.name: Serranilla Bank
ne-SER.note: Awarded to Colombia by the International Court of Justice in 2012.

ne-SCR.name: Scarborough Shoal
ne-SCR.note: Controlled by Chinese coast guard ships since a 2012 standoff; claimed by the Philippines.

abkhazia.name: Abkhazia
abkhazia.note: Self-governing since the 1992-93 war, with a permanent Russian military presence.

south-ossetia.name: South Ossetia
south-ossetia.note: Self-governing since the early 1990s; Russian forces have been based there since the 2008 war.

transnistria.name: Transnistria
transnistria.note: Self-governing since the 1992 war, with a Russian garrison.

ukraine-occupied.name: Russian-occupied Ukraine
ukraine-occupied.note: Crimea (occupied since 2014) and the parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts held since 2022: about a fifth of Ukraine. Russia claims to have annexed Crimea and four oblasts. Drawn as the Ukrainian municipalities (OpenStreetMap level 3, via geoBoundaries) that are mostly occupied on DeepStateMap's map, so the line is approximate at the scale of individual municipalities.

sources.title: Chatham House: How a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire could imperil Ukrainian and European security (May 2026)

ukraine-gray.name: Gray zone along the front
ukraine-gray.note: Municipalities mostly in the zone DeepStateMap marks as unknown status, where neither side has established control.

west-bank.name: West Bank and East Jerusalem
west-bank.note: Under Israeli military occupation since 1967; East Jerusalem was annexed by Israel. The Palestinian Authority administers civil affairs in Areas A and B (about 40% of the West Bank).

gaza-israeli.name: Israeli-held Gaza
gaza-israeli.note: East of the 'yellow line' set by the October 2025 ceasefire, which Israel has since pushed westward: Israeli estimates put its share of the Strip at about 63% in October 2026.

sources.title: CBC: Israel's yellow line in Gaza is moving
Israel Hayom: Behind the Yellow Line (8 October 2026)

gaza-hamas.name: Hamas-held Gaza
gaza-hamas.note: West of the yellow line: Gaza City's western neighborhoods, the central camps, and western Khan Younis and al-Mawasi. Hand-drawn approximation of a line that moves.

golan.name: Golan Heights
golan.note: Held by Israel since 1967 and annexed in 1981; the United States recognized the annexation in 2019, but nearly all other states consider it occupied Syrian territory. Includes the Shebaa Farms, claimed by Lebanon.

syria-buffer.name: Syrian buffer zone and Mount Hermon
syria-buffer.note: Israeli forces entered the UN-patrolled buffer zone after Assad's fall in December 2024 and said they would stay; I couldn't confirm their 2026 positions.

sources.title: AAP: Israeli troops to stay in buffer zone inside Syria

suwayda.name: Suwayda
suwayda.note: Run by Druze factions under a single National Guard aligned with Sheikh al-Hijri since the July 2025 massacres; the government still holds the province's western and far eastern edges.

sources.title: Syria Direct: Suwayda stands at a crossroads
UN Syria Commission report on Suwayda (March 2026)

yemen-houthi.name: Houthi-held Yemen
yemen-houthi.note: The north and west, home to most of Yemen's population. Drawn at the district level; the front has barely moved since the April 2022 truce. After the separatist STC's December 2025 offensive collapsed and the group dissolved in January 2026, the south is held by government and Saudi-backed forces.

sources.title: MERIP: Yemen After the Saudi-Emirati Split (July 2026)
Middle East Institute: Riyadh takes the helm in Yemen

libya-east.name: Eastern and southern Libya
libya-east.note: Held by Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army, with the parallel House of Representatives government; the lines have been stable since the 2020 ceasefire, with Turkish forces in the west and Russian ones in Haftar's territory deterring either side.

sources.title: Kuwait Times: Libyan National Army conducts grand exercises

sudan-rsf.name: RSF-held Sudan
sudan-rsf.note: Almost all of Darfur, where El Fasher fell in October 2025, and nearly all of West Kordofan, where Babanusa's army base fell in December 2025.

sources.title: Sudans Post: Territorial control map as of 25 September 2026
Al Jazeera: The battle for Kordofan (1 October 2026)
Mada Masr: RSF seizes military's last stronghold in West Kordofan

sudan-jebel-marra.name: Jebel Marra and Tawila
sudan-jebel-marra.note: The SLM faction of Abdel Wahid al-Nur holds parts of these localities, outside both army and RSF control.

sources.title: Sudans Post: Territorial control map as of 25 September 2026

sudan-splmn.name: Nuba Mountains and southern Blue Nile
sudan-splmn.note: SPLM-North (al-Hilu) has held the core of the Nuba Mountains since 2011 and, with the RSF, parts of southern Blue Nile. Kadugli and Dilling remain army-held under siege.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Is the Sudanese army gaining momentum against the RSF? (4 October 2026)
Sudans Post: Territorial control map as of 25 September 2026

sudan-kordofan-front.name: North Kordofan front
sudan-kordofan-front.note: Bara has changed hands repeatedly; the army took Sodari on 25 September and says it took al-Mazroub in early October.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Sudan's army says it captured RSF stronghold in North Kordofan (2 October 2026)
Sudan Tribune: Sudan army recaptures 11 areas in North Kordofan

abyei.name: Abyei
abyei.note: Claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan and patrolled by UN peacekeepers (UNISFA) since 2011.

kivu-m23.name: AFC/M23-held Kivu
kivu-m23.note: Goma (January 2025), Bukavu (February 2025) and the surrounding territories. Peace talks under the Doha framework agreed a roadmap in August 2026, but fighting continues.

sources.title: Critical Threats: Congo War Security Review (25 September 2026)
Al Jazeera: DR Congo, M23 rebels agree on roadmap for peace talks

kivu-front.name: Walikale and Uvira
kivu-front.note: Contested between AFC/M23 and the army and its allies; positions change hands week to week.

sources.title: Critical Threats: Congo War Security Review (25 September 2026)

puntland.name: Puntland
puntland.note: Has governed itself without recognizing the federal government since 2024, pending constitutional changes; it is fighting Islamic State in the Cal Miskaad mountains.

sources.title: Horn Review: US relations with Somaliland, Puntland, and Jubaland (August 2026)

ssc-khatumo.name: Sool and Buhodle (SSC-Khatumo)
ssc-khatumo.note: Taken from Somaliland by SSC-Khatumo forces in 2023; now a federal member state (North Eastern State) aligned with Mogadishu. Somaliland still claims it.

jubaland.name: Jubaland
jubaland.note: Holds Kismayo and the Lower Juba towns; broke with the federal government after its contested 2024 election and repelled federal forces.

sources.title: Horn Review: US relations with Somaliland, Puntland, and Jubaland (August 2026)

shabaab-juba.name: Middle Juba
shabaab-juba.note: Al-Shabaab's heartland, held for the group's entire existence; it also controls much of rural southern and central Somalia (see the insurgent-presence layer).

sources.title: CTC Sentinel: Somalia at a Crossroads

rakhine-aa.name: Rakhine and Paletwa
rakhine-aa.note: About 90% of Rakhine State (14 of 17 townships) plus Paletwa in Chin State; the junta holds Sittwe, Kyaukphyu and Manaung.

sources.title: The Diplomat: For the Arakan Army, Recognition Must Be Earned (July 2026)
Wikipedia: Territory of the Arakan Army

wa-state.name: Wa State
wa-state.note: The northern Wa region (the Wa Self-Administered Division). The UWSA also holds a separate southern area along the Thai border, not drawn here.

sources.title: Irrawaddy: Wa become first ethnic force to congratulate Min Aung Hlaing on presidency

mongla.name: Mongla
mongla.note: Special Region 4, self-administered under a ceasefire since 1989.

kokang.name: Kokang and Kutkai
kokang.note: The Kokang region since January 2024, and Kutkai since March 2026; the MNDAA returned Lashio to the junta in 2025 under Chinese pressure.

taang.name: Ta'ang areas
taang.note: The junta demanded in May 2026 that the TNLA withdraw to Namhsan and Mantong alone; it had not done so.

sources.title: IMNA: TNLA under pressure to withdraw from captured towns (May 2026)
Irrawaddy: Myanmar regime tells TNLA to surrender another four towns

taiwan-prc.name: Taiwan
taiwan-prc.note: Claimed by the People's Republic of China, which has never governed it.

kosovo-srb.name: Kosovo
kosovo-srb.note: Claimed by Serbia since Kosovo declared independence in 2008.

ncyprus-cyp.name: Northern Cyprus
ncyprus-cyp.note: Claimed by the Republic of Cyprus.

crimea-ukr.name: Crimea
crimea-ukr.note: Claimed by Ukraine; occupied and annexed by Russia in 2014.

sadr-mar.name: Sahrawi Free Zone
sadr-mar.note: Claimed by Morocco as part of its southern provinces.

wsahara-sah.name: Western Sahara (Moroccan-held)
wsahara-sah.note: Claimed by the Sahrawi Republic; held by Morocco west of the berm.

kashmir-pak-held-ind.name: Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan
kashmir-pak-held-ind.note: Held by Pakistan; claimed by India.

kashmir-chn-held-ind.name: Aksai Chin and Shaksgam
kashmir-chn-held-ind.note: Held by China; claimed by India.

kashmir-ind-held-pak.name: Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh
kashmir-ind-held-pak.note: Held by India; claimed by Pakistan.

siachen-pak.name: Siachen Glacier
siachen-pak.note: Held by India since 1984; claimed by Pakistan.

arunachal-chn.name: Arunachal Pradesh and other areas
arunachal-chn.note: Held by India; claimed by China.

bhutan-chn.name: Northern Bhutan
bhutan-chn.note: Held by Bhutan; claimed by China.

kalapani-npl.name: Kalapani
kalapani-npl.note: Held by India; claimed by Nepal.

golan-syr.name: Golan Heights
golan-syr.note: Held by Israel since 1967; claimed by Syria.

shebaa-lbn.name: Shebaa Farms
shebaa-lbn.note: Held by Israel; claimed by Lebanon.

ejerusalem-psx.name: East Jerusalem
ejerusalem-psx.note: Held and annexed by Israel; claimed by Palestine.

kurils-jpn.name: Southern Kuril Islands
kurils-jpn.note: Held by Russia since 1945; claimed by Japan as its Northern Territories.

falklands-arg.name: Falkland Islands
falklands-arg.note: Held by the United Kingdom; claimed by Argentina.

sgeorgia-arg.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
sgeorgia-arg.note: Held by the United Kingdom; claimed by Argentina.

essequibo-ven.name: Guayana Esequiba
essequibo-ven.note: Held by Guyana; claimed by Venezuela, which declared it a Venezuelan state in 2024.

gibraltar-esp.name: Gibraltar
gibraltar-esp.note: Held by the United Kingdom; claimed by Spain.

ceuta-melilla-mar.name: Ceuta, Melilla, and Spanish islets
ceuta-melilla-mar.note: Held by Spain; claimed by Morocco.

paracels-vnm.name: Paracel Islands
paracels-vnm.note: Held by China since 1974; claimed by Vietnam.

paracels-twn.name: Paracel Islands
paracels-twn.note: Held by China; claimed by Taiwan.

spratlys-chn.name: Spratly Islands
spratlys-chn.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; China claims them all.

spratlys-vnm.name: Spratly Islands
spratlys-vnm.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; Vietnam claims them all.

spratlys-phl.name: Spratly Islands
spratlys-phl.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; the Philippines claims part of them.

spratlys-twn.name: Spratly Islands
spratlys-twn.note: Occupied in parts by five claimants; Taiwan claims them all.

scarborough-phl.name: Scarborough Shoal
scarborough-phl.note: Controlled by Chinese coast guard ships since 2012; claimed by the Philippines.

senkaku-chn.name: Senkaku Islands
senkaku-chn.note: Held by Japan; claimed by China as the Diaoyu Islands.

senkaku-twn.name: Senkaku Islands
senkaku-twn.note: Held by Japan; claimed by Taiwan.

dokdo-jpn.name: Liancourt Rocks
dokdo-jpn.note: Held by South Korea as Dokdo; claimed by Japan as Takeshima.

tunbs-are.name: Abu Musa and the Tunbs
tunbs-are.note: Held by Iran since 1971; claimed by the UAE.

halaib-sdn.name: Hala'ib Triangle
halaib-sdn.note: Held by Egypt; claimed by Sudan.

ilemi-sds.name: Ilemi Triangle
ilemi-sds.note: Administered by Kenya; claimed by South Sudan.

kafia-kingi-sds.name: Kafia Kingi
kafia-kingi-sds.note: Held by Sudan; claimed by South Sudan.

belize-gtm.name: Southern Belize
belize-gtm.note: Held by Belize; claimed by Guatemala, pending at the International Court of Justice.

guantanamo-cub.name: Guantánamo Bay
guantanamo-cub.note: Leased to the United States since 1903; Cuba considers the lease invalid.

mayotte-com.name: Mayotte
mayotte-com.note: Held by France; claimed by Comoros.

scattered-mdg.name: Scattered Islands
scattered-mdg.note: Held by France; claimed by Madagascar.

tromelin-mus.name: Tromelin Island
tromelin-mus.note: Held by France; claimed by Mauritius.

suriname-guy.name: Tigri Area
suriname-guy.note: Held by Guyana; claimed by Suriname.

suriname-guf.name: Lawa Headwaters
suriname-guf.note: Held by France (French Guiana); claimed by Suriname.

olivenza-prt.name: Olivenza
olivenza-prt.note: Held by Spain; claimed by Portugal.

matthew-hunter-vut.name: Matthew and Hunter Islands
matthew-hunter-vut.note: Held by France (New Caledonia); claimed by Vanuatu.

wake-mhl.name: Wake Island
wake-mhl.note: Held by the United States; claimed by the Marshall Islands.

navassa-hti.name: Navassa Island
navassa-hti.note: Held by the United States; claimed by Haiti.

artigas-ury.name: Corner of Artigas
artigas-ury.note: Held by Brazil; claimed by Uruguay.

doumera-dji.name: Doumeira Islands
doumera-dji.note: Held by Eritrea; claimed by Djibouti.

prk-kor.name: North Korea
prk-kor.note: South Korea's constitution claims the whole peninsula.

oblasts-rus.name: Rest of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson
oblasts-rus.note: Russia claims to have annexed these four oblasts in full in September 2022, including the parts it has never held, among them the cities of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Russian annexation of Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts

palestine-psx.name: West Bank and Gaza
palestine-psx.note: The territory of the State of Palestine as recognized by most UN members.

ssc-sol.name: Sool and Buhodle
ssc-sol.note: Claimed by Somaliland, which lost Las Anod to SSC-Khatumo forces in 2023.

aq-brazilian-antarctica-unofficial.name: Brazilian Antarctica (unofficial)
aq-brazilian-antarctica-unofficial.note: Unofficial zone of interest, not a formal claim.

aq-argentine-antarctica.name: Argentine Antarctica
aq-argentine-antarctica.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

aq-australian-antarctic-territory.name: Australian Antarctic Territory
aq-australian-antarctic-territory.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

aq-ross-dependency.name: Ross Dependency
aq-ross-dependency.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

aq-ant-rctica.name: Antárctica
aq-ant-rctica.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

aq-queen-maud-land.name: Queen Maud Land
aq-queen-maud-land.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959). Southern boundary of Norwegian claim is undefined.

aq-ad-lie-land.name: Adélie Land
aq-ad-lie-land.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

aq-british-antarctic-territory.name: British Antarctic Territory
aq-british-antarctic-territory.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

aq-peter-i-island.name: Peter I Island
aq-peter-i-island.note: Claim held in abeyance by the Antarctic Treaty (1959).

shabaab-south.name: Southern and central Somalia
shabaab-south.note: Holds much of the countryside and taxes trade even in government-held towns; estimates put its control at around 30% of Somalia's land.

sources.title: War on the Rocks: Flailing State, the resurgence of al-Shabaab

kachin.name: Kachin State
kachin.note: The KIA holds much of rural Kachin State and several towns, and is pressing junta positions around Bhamo; the junta holds Myitkyina.

sources.title: Myanmar Peace Monitor: The junta's campaign to recapture resistance-controlled towns

chin.name: Chin State
chin.note: Chin resistance forces hold most of the state's towns and countryside.

sagaing-magway.name: Sagaing and Magway
sagaing-magway.note: People's Defense Forces loyal to the National Unity Government contest much of the dry zone; the junta imposed martial law on dozens of townships here in April 2026.

sources.title: Malay Mail: Myanmar junta imposes military control over 60 townships (April 2026)

karenni.name: Karenni (Kayah) State
karenni.note: Karenni resistance forces hold much of the state, though the junta has retaken some towns since 2025.

karen.name: Karen (Kayin) State
karen.note: The KNU and allied forces control large rural areas along the Thai border.

jnim-mali.name: Central and western Mali
jnim-mali.note: JNIM controls much of the countryside, besieges towns, and blockaded fuel supplies to Bamako in late 2025.

jnim-burkina.name: Northern and eastern Burkina Faso
jnim-burkina.note: JNIM operates across roughly half of Burkina Faso, blockading many towns that the junta nominally holds.

issp.name: Ménaka, Gao, Tillabéri and Tahoua
issp.note: Islamic State Sahel dominates the Ménaka region and the borderlands of western Niger.

fla.name: Kidal region
fla.note: Tuareg separatists lost Kidal town to the army in 2023 but remain active in the desert, notably around Tinzaouaten.

iswap.name: Lake Chad and northern Borno
iswap.note: ISWAP holds the Lake Chad islands and much of northern Borno's countryside.

jas.name: Sambisa and the Mandara Mountains
jas.note: Boko Haram's JAS faction operates from the Sambisa forest and the Mandara Mountains.

fano.name: Amhara
fano.note: Fano militias have fought the federal government since 2023 and hold much of rural Amhara.

cabo-delgado.name: Cabo Delgado
cabo-delgado.note: Islamic State Mozambique remains active despite Rwandan and Mozambican operations.

ambazonia.name: Northwest and Southwest Cameroon
ambazonia.note: Anglophone separatists have fought for an independent 'Ambazonia' since 2017.

ttp.name: Former tribal areas
ttp.note: The Pakistani Taliban has resurged in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's former tribal districts since 2021.

balochistan.name: Balochistan
balochistan.note: Baloch separatists stage frequent attacks across the province, including the 2025 Jaffar Express hijacking.

eln.name: Catatumbo and Arauca
eln.note: The ELN has dominated these border departments since its 2025 Catatumbo offensive.

emc.name: Cauca and Guaviare
emc.note: FARC dissident factions control rural areas and coca routes.

haiti.name: Ouest and Artibonite
haiti.note: The Viv Ansanm gang coalition controls most of Port-au-Prince and much of the Artibonite valley.

splaio.name: Upper Nile and Jonglei
splaio.note: Fighting between the government and opposition forces resumed in 2025 after Riek Machar's arrest.

adf.name: Beni, Lubero and Ituri
adf.note: The Islamic State-affiliated ADF carries out frequent massacres of civilians.
